children: Malaysia's fiscal deficit is forecast to narrow to 3.4% of GDP in 2027 from an estimated 3.6% in 2026, as revenue growth supports gradual fiscal consolidation, BMI says in a note. The government is targeting a deficit of 3.3% next year. Higher oil prices and stronger economic activity are expected to boost petroleum-related income and tax collections. However, elevated energy costs and household assistance will keep spending high, with subsidies and social assistance budgeted at 72.7 billion ringgit in 2027, BMI says. Development spending is projected to fall for a third consecutive year, potentially weighing on longer-term productivity and innovation, it adds. A prolonged U.S.-Iran conflict could increase subsidy costs and widen the deficit, BMI says, adding that severe El Nino conditions may require additional agricultural support. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
